author: Temminck & Schlegel, 1844
summary: 우리나라에 드물게 찾아오는 겨울철새로, 농경지와 평지, 간척지, 트인 땅에서 지낸다. 부드러운 날갯짓으로 날며 쥐와 곤충, 작은 새 등을 잡아먹는다. 세계 개체 수에 관한 구체적인 자료는 없으나, 주식인 설치류의 수와 개체 수가 관계있을 것으로 본다. 티베트, 러시아, 몽골 등지에서 번식한다.

art.subject: Upland Buzzard (Buteo hemilasius), adult pale morph, as seen over Korean farmland in winter: head whitish with fine dark streaks; neck and breast whitish, streaked rufous-brown; upperparts and upperwing coverts warm brown with pale buff feather fringes; a large whitish patch at the base of the primaries on the upperwing; flanks, belly sides and thighs dark brown, forming dark 'trousers' and a dark U around a paler centre to the belly; underwing whitish with rufous-brown lesser coverts, large blackish carpal patches and black wingtips; tail whitish to pale buff, finely barred grey, without a broad dark terminal band. Short hooked dark bill with a yellow cere; legs feathered on the front for more than half their length; bare toes yellow.
art.pose: flying low over open fields with supple wingbeats, searching for prey
art.scene: Korean winter open farmland and flat reclaimed land under a wide sky; no people, buildings or text
views: adult pale morph, side view perched upright: rounded whitish head lightly streaked, short hooked dark bill with a yellow cere, whitish breast streaked rufous-brown, dark brown flanks and thighs, warm brown upperparts with pale fringes, legs feathered for most of their length, yellow toes

adult pale morph, in flight seen squarely from below: long broad fingered wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, whitish barred flight feathers, blackish wingtips and trailing edge, rufous-brown coverts with dark carpal patches, pale breast, dark flanks and thighs forming a U around the paler belly, feet under the tail

adult pale morph, in flight seen squarely from above: long broad wings with fingered tips spread straight out to the sides to their full span, brown upperwing coverts, wide white flash at the base of the primaries, dark wingtips, whitish head, pale tail
art.build: The largest buzzard in Korea, clearly bigger and longer-winged than Eastern Buzzard, approaching a small eagle in bulk. Heavy body, rounded head, short hooked bill. Long, broad wings with well-fingered tips. Tail medium length, fan-shaped when spread. Soars and glides on wings raised in a shallow V, often hovers over fields, and flies with slow, supple, elastic wingbeats.
avoid: Do not paint a white tail with a broad dark terminal band — that is Rough-legged Buzzard (Buteo lagopus).
Do not paint a dark brown head and an evenly barred brown tail like Eastern Buzzard (Buteo japonicus).
Do not paint fully bare legs; the front of the tarsus is feathered.
Do not paint an eagle with a long heavy bill or a long wedge-shaped tail.
